CFD_Automation · Stage 1 · geometry · code 0.5.0

Wing Generator

Eighteen numbers go in; one exact wing surface comes out, measured, labelled and checked. One generator and one YAML file make BWB, cranked and tapered wings, sized like real Class I and II UAVs. Every later stage (mesh, solver, data) reads only this surface.

At a glanceFix before Stage 2Design decisionsReal wings and ReThe 18 numbersChecks and resultsOpen decisionsWhat it cannot makePublished wingsCommands

At a glance

In

18 numbers + a wing type

From configs/wing.yaml: chords, spans, sweeps, twists, dihedrals, and an airfoil per station. Types: BWB, conventional (cranked), tapered.

Out

One surface, checked

Upper, lower and trailing-edge base, read as upper(u, v). Plus measured values, labels, four refusing checks, a hash, IGES.

Evidence

438 of 438 wings pass

Sampled wings, both types, 0 refused (built with code 0.5.0). 7 of 7 published wings verified. Tests: 122 pass without pyGeo, 11 more need pyGeo (run 28 Oct 2026).

Verdict

Ready for Stage 2 after three fixes

Not yet "any wing": straight panels only, no airfoil shape variable. Sets must be rebuilt: no, they match the current code.

Fix before Stage 2

Each fix changes the hashes, so do all three before one rebuild. Done on 29 Oct 2026: the unrealistic conventional set (tapered type and per-panel chords).

  1. One dihedral variable does nothing.Four station dihedrals become three panel angles. [0, 3, 3, 6], [3, 0, 6, 3] and [1.5, 1.5, 4.5, 4.5] give the same wing to 0.003°. The gate compares with the derived angle, so it passes anyway. Do: Use three panel dihedrals.
  2. The hash ignores code changes.It uses __version__, a string bumped by hand. Code changes between bumps leave the hash the same. Do: Hash the source files (or the git commit).
  3. The loft has sharp kinks at b1, b2 and the switch sections.Correct for straight panels, but the S8 mesher does not place stations at the breaks. Flat mesh faces would then cut the corner, about 0.5 % of chord (a rough estimate). Do: Stage 2 must put a mesh station exactly at every station_v. No change here; put it in the Stage 2 prompt.

One wing, step by step

Seven steps: design vector, planform, sections, twist and dihedral, trailing edge, loft, measure-label-check. Example: a BWB with every variable at mid-range.

Design decisions

Every choice behind the generator, with its reason and what it rests on. Details: geometry/decisions/ and Stage 0_Decisions/OPEN_DECISIONS.md.

Planform
D11Exact straight panelsLeading and trailing edges are straight lines through b0–b3. Chords and sweeps equal the vector exactly.The old AERIS spline put the b2 chord up to 20 % off; a 12°/6°/6° wing came out 7.9°/7.9°/6.5°.Measured

Sections, twist, dihedral
D14Vertical sectionsEvery section is parallel to the symmetry plane and twisted about its leading edge.The root then stays in y = 0 with any dihedral, so the two halves never cross. AERIS rolled the root, so it had to force zero dihedral there. Cost: on a panel with dihedral Γ the true thickness is cos Γ smaller (1.5 % at 10°).Our choice
D15Height from dihedral Fixz = ∫ tan(dihedral) dy, dihedral linear between stations (AERIS formula). Each straight panel gets one dihedral, the mean.Exact and independent of how the span is cut. But 4 station values give only 3 panel angles: see fix 1.Our choice
D16TwistExact at the four stations; between them it follows the straight panel.Straight panels and linear twist cannot both hold. Difference 0.1–0.3 % of chord at the trailing edge.Measured

D19One way to read every fileLeading edge = the point farthest from the trailing-edge midpoint; unit chord; both sides resampled on cosine x, in √x.The nose tangent is square to the chord, and every section has the same points, so the loft can join them.Our choice

Real wings and the Reynolds number

Your rule (29 Oct 2026): take the sizes from real Class I and II UAVs, compute the Re they fly at, and if it does not reach 5 × 10⁶, lower the top Re level instead of stretching the wings. Data and links: configs/real_uavs.yaml; check: scripts/real_uav_check.py.

Real wings fly at

Re 1.2 × 10⁵ – 2.1 × 10⁶

Lowest: Black Swift S0 cruising at 3,048 m. Highest: AAI Pioneer at top speed, sea level. Mean chord = wing area / span.

So the top Re level

5 × 10⁶ → 2 × 10⁶

No wing of our families reaches 5 × 10⁶. Only the Sperwer does: a delta wing, outside our families, area from a secondary site. Levels now 3 × 10⁵, 1.5 × 10⁶, 2 × 10⁶.

Generator covers them

all real wings

Each real wing with a published area has a generated wing within 10 % in span and mean chord. Every Class I span is inside too (sourced and HCDI database). BWB span 0.9–3.5 m, mean chord 0.17–0.47 m; conventional span 0.6–7.0 m, mean chord 0.09–0.58 m.

Gap

Class II: 10 wings outside

Spans 5.2–10.9 m (Hermes 450, Watchkeeper, Karayel, Mohajer-6, Shahed 191, …), none with a published area. At 36–40 m/s cruise, a mean chord above about 0.8 m puts them above Re 2 × 10⁶, so the top level may rise again.

Spans from the HCDI UAS database (v13)

794 entries; 76 fixed-wing Class I–II; 18 give a span; none gives a wing area, so these rows test the span range only. Four Class I flying wings (3.1–3.5 m) were longer than the BWB range, so the BWB semi-span now goes to 1.75 m. Class II wings (5–11 m) stay outside until their areas are found.

Database weak points. No source per row. 28 rows share cruise 35 m/s, endurance 6 h and range 100 km (look like defaults); on 8 rows cruise is above top speed. Orlan-10 is listed as Class II at 18 kg, Puma LE as a flying wing, XQ-58 Valkyrie (a jet) as Class II; Zala Z-16's maker field names a microchip company. Only span, class, MTOW and payload are used here.

Checks and results

Gate 1 · vector → loft

Measured on the loft: chords within 0.1 %, sweeps 0.1°, twist 0.2°, dihedral 0.2°.

Gate 2 · trailing edge

Thickness equals the rule at every section, within 1 µm.

Gate 3 · validity

Sections closed, upper never below lower, root flat in y = 0 within 1e-9 m, chords positive.

Gate 4 · repeatability

Two builds give the same surface hash.

A wing that fails any gate is not written; its row keeps the gate and the reason. The fifth check, mesh on the loft within 1e-9 m, belongs to Stage 2.

Open decisions

Choices made to keep going that still need your call.

  • Class II wing areas. Ten Class II wings (5.2–10.9 m span, from the sourced table and your HCDI database) are outside the span range and have no published wing area. A mean chord above about 0.8 m would put them above Re 2 × 10⁶. Find the areas (Jane's, papers), then widen and settle the top Re level.
  • Re levels. Now 3 × 10⁵, 1.5 × 10⁶, 2 × 10⁶: the upper two are close. Move the middle to about 6 × 10⁵? Mini Class I wings fly at 1.2–2 × 10⁵, below the lowest level.
  • Label for slim tailless wings. 42 % of the bwb-type wings are now slim flying wings without a centre body; the rule labels them "conventional", which reads like "has a tail". Rename to "flying wing"?
  • Mixed shares. BWB 0.5, cranked 0.25, tapered 0.25. Keep?
  • Shape ranges. Sweeps, twists, dihedrals and tapers have no source yet. Take them from real wings too?
  • Trailing-edge floor. Confirm 0.5 mm / 1.0 mm with the builder. Run the 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 % sensitivity once CFD works.
  • Airfoil search order. Project folder → AERIS database → NACA formula. Keep? 22 database files are refused.
  • NACA 25118 trailing edge. Made from the formula (open edge, 0.38 %). OpenVSP may close it differently. Check with a BlendedNet STEP file.
  • NASA CRM. Four stations and stand-in sections: a shape check only, or add a many-station mode for drag validation?
  • BlendedNet twist and dihedral. Set to zero because neither paper states them. Accept?
  • Which published wing first. RIBES is the only in-regime case; M6 and CRM are transonic.
  • RIBES trailing edge. The fitted section has 0.26 %; the model measures 0.38–0.66 %. Rebuild before any drag comparison?
  • Outside proof. Only the M6 is checked against its own CAD (max 0.011 % of chord). BlendedNet, CRM and RIBES need their surface files.

What it cannot make (yet)

  • Straight edges only, three panels at most. No curved BWB centre body, no elliptic planform, no fourth panel.
  • Airfoil shape is not a variable. Any named file can be used, and a station can draw from a list, but thickness and camber are not sampled continuously. The default sets use one section per station (t/c 11–15 %).
  • No winglets, rounded or raked tips, fuselage, gaps. Dihedral is at most 10° (BWB) and 6° (conventional).
  • Class I and small Class II only. Spans reach 3.5 m (tailless) and 7 m (with tail). Class II wings of 5–11 m (Hermes 450, Watchkeeper, Shahed 191) are outside until their areas are found.
  • 0 refusals at the corners. The space is too safe to show where anything breaks. Robustness must be shown on the mesher, with lofts it has never seen (primer Track 5).
  • Published wings: M6 and CRM are transonic (phase 1 stops at Mach 0.3). CRM is approximate. BlendedNet twist and dihedral are guessed as zero. Every tip is a flat cut, including the M6's rounded one.

Published wings it rebuilds

Each frame is a wing rebuilt by the same generator, with the same loft and checks as the sampled wings. BlendedNet wings are made directly from the BlendedNet parameters.

Commands

cd CFD_Automation/geometry
python -m cfdauto.geometry.sample                                    # write the sets
python -m cfdauto.geometry.build --type bwb --set training --index 7  # one wing
python -m cfdauto.geometry.build --all                               # every training, corner, reference wing (pyGeo)
python -m cfdauto.geometry.published_wings --build all               # M6, RIBES, CRM, BlendedNet (pyGeo)
python scripts/verify_geometry.py                                    # is the surface the intended wing?
python -m pytest -m "not pygeo"                                      # tests without pyGeo
python scripts/make_generator_visuals.py                             # the GIFs and pictures
python scripts/make_generator_page.py                                # this page
